$comment: CESIDR liturgical traditions: draft canonical IDs for the liturgical traditions from which the rites of the Churches sui iuris arise. Referenced from data/churches.json as the value of each Church's `tradition` field. CCEO can. 28 §2 names five: 'The rites treated in this code, unless otherwise stated, are those which arise from the Alexandrian, Antiochene, Armenian, Chaldean and Constantinopolitan traditions.' The Latin tradition is not among them — the CCEO governs the Eastern Churches only — and is minted here so that the Latin Church can carry a `tradition` like every other entry. Note the distinction of CCEO can. 27 and 28: a Church sui iuris is a community joined by a hierarchy, a rite is a patrimony; several Churches share one tradition. All IDs are drafts pending committee review; the `trad:` prefix is a placeholder.

entries.note: Not among the five traditions of CCEO can. 28 §2, which treats the Eastern Churches only. Minted so that the Latin Church carries a tradition like every other entry. Also styled the Western or Roman tradition.
The CCEO's own name for it is Constantinopolitan; Byzantine is the usual English style. By far the most widely shared tradition — fourteen of the twenty-four Churches sui iuris arise from it.
Comprises the Coptic and the Ge'ez (Ethiopic) liturgical families.
Also styled West Syriac. The Maronite Church has its own distinct usage within it.

The CCEO's own name for it is Chaldean; East Syriac is the usual descriptive style. The slug follows the descriptive form to avoid collision with the Chaldean Catholic Church (esi:chaldean), which is one of the two Churches arising from it — see open question 3 in docs/schema-proposal.md.
The only tradition represented by a single Church sui iuris.
